acceptance: `make heavy-run WAIT=10 CMD=...` on a refusing host waits, re-samples, and runs the command once admitted, or exits 76 with the last admission report after 10 minutes.
While waiting it does not hold the host lock, shown by a second heavy run acquiring it.
`docs/agent/heavy-work.md` documents the option and says callers must not write their own retry loops.
description:
Gap. On 2026-11-12 heavy-work admission refused for over three hours (memory pressure level 2). `make heavy-run` exits 76 immediately, so two separate agents each wrote their own retry loop (a shell watcher retrying every 5 minutes for 8 hours, and a subagent retrying six times), which the guide otherwise discourages. A waiter that ends up admitted while the lock holder changes also has no fairness guarantee.

Expected: an opt-in `WAIT=<minutes>` (or equivalent) on `make heavy-run` that re-samples admission at a fixed interval up to the budget, holds no lock while waiting, and exits with the existing refusal code and report when the budget ends.

Guardrails: default behaviour unchanged (refuse at once). No way to force admission through this option; `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force` stays owner-approved. The watchdog stays on.
